top_news.title: Agents, Workers - Choose OAuth scopes for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server
top_news.dek: Cloudflare now supports optional OAuth scopes for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server, allowing for more granular permission control.
top_news.brief: Users can now selectively grant or revoke optional OAuth scopes during the authorization process for Wrangler and the Cloudflare API MCP server. The updated consent dialog includes an 'Edit Permissions' feature, enabling developers to restrict access to specific resources while keeping required scopes enabled.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare OAuth consent dialog showing the Edit Permissions interface.

top_news.title: NanoGPT Speedrun Frontier
top_news.dek: PRIME Intellect conducted 153 autonomous training runs across 18 frontier models to benchmark and optimize nanoGPT performance.
top_news.brief: The research team executed a series of autonomous training runs to analyze the nanoGPT optimizer. The study focuses on identifying performance bottlenecks and efficiency gains in training frontier-scale models.

top_news.title: llm 0.33
top_news.dek: The llm CLI tool version 0.33 upgrades to the OpenAI Python library 3.x and adds per-call API key support for embedding operations.
top_news.brief: This release migrates the HTTP client dependency to httpx2 and updates the underlying OpenAI library. Additionally, the embed and embed-multi commands now support the --key flag, allowing users to pass API keys directly to plugins without modifying global state.
top_news.image_alt: Terminal interface showing llm CLI output

top_news.title: Cloudflare Announces Kitesurf, a Browser Engine for Agents
top_news.dek: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a lightweight, WebAssembly-based browser engine designed for automated agent workloads.
top_news.brief: Kitesurf runs on Cloudflare Workers, providing a resource-efficient alternative to full Chromium instances. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol, enabling compatibility with existing automation frameworks like Playwright and Puppeteer while reducing overhead.

primary.title: Study explains why AI agents benefit from "skills" and when they fail
primary.summary: A study from researchers at Princeton University and UC San Diego finds that so-called skills make AI agents better mainly through structured workflows, not through added knowledge. But as the skill library grows, agents have a harder and harder time finding the right set of instructions. The article Study explains why AI agents benefit from "skills" and when they fail appeared first on The Decoder.

primary.title: Psychological methods reveal major weaknesses in AI security testing
primary.summary: Researchers at the UK AI Security Institute used psychometric methods to show that popular safety benchmarks for language models don't measure one consistent trait. Blanket blocking of requests can artificially inflate a safety score even as the model gets less useful day to day. The study also offers a method for catching models that act more cautious during tests than they do in normal use. The article Psychological methods reveal major weaknesses in AI security testing appeared first on The Decoder.
